summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and hepatocellular carcinoma on the transplant list, was admitted for evaluation of hematemesis. He reported four episodes of vomiting blood, nausea, chest pain, and shortness of breath over several days. He was hemodynamically stable with a hemoglobin within his baseline. An EGD revealed gastritis, duodenitis, and polypoid lesions without active bleeding or varices. He received IV pantoprazole, transitioned to high-dose oral omeprazole, and was started on ciprofloxacin and metronidazole for prophylaxis. His symptoms resolved during the hospitalization, and he was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans with his hepatologist and primary care provider.
